title: UN Chief Issues Final Warning as COP31 Climate Summit Nears End
subtitle: As world leaders depart Turkey, the focus shifts to the future of global energy and the fight against fossil fuels.

summary.en: UN Secretary-General António Guterres delivered an emotional final address at the COP31 summit in Turkey. He warned that peace is impossible on a warming planet and urged nations to follow scientific facts. Meanwhile, California Governor Gavin Newsom expressed strong support for a global move away from fossil fuels. A coalition of over 50 nations is now working on independent plans to switch to clean energy. The summit is expected to conclude with a final agreement on energy transition targets.
summary.zh: 聯合國秘書長古特瑞斯在土耳其舉行的 COP31 峰會上發表了感人的告別演說。他警告在暖化的地球上不可能實現和平，並敦促各國遵循科學事實。與此同時，加州州長紐森對全球擺脫化石燃料的行動表達了強烈支持。目前，一個由五十多個國家組成的聯盟正致力於制定獨立計畫，以轉向潔淨能源。預計峰會將以達成能源轉型目標的最終協議作為總結。

paragraphs.en: As the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, draws to a close, United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres has delivered a final, powerful message to the world. In his last climate summit speech before leaving office, Guterres warned that the climate crisis is spinning out of control. He told the audience that the world cannot build peace on a burning planet, noting that climate disasters often destroy progress in fighting poverty and threaten the safety of future generations.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著在土耳其安塔利亞（Antalya）舉行的 COP31 氣候峰會即將落幕，聯合國秘書長古特瑞斯（António Guterres）向全球發表了最後且強而有力的訊息。在他卸任前最後一次的氣候峰會演說中，古特瑞斯警告氣候危機已失控。他向與會者表示，世界無法在一個燃燒的星球上建立和平，並指出氣候災難往往會摧毀消除貧困的進展，並威脅到未來世代的安全。

paragraphs.en: According to The Guardian, Guterres has been a very direct leader regarding climate change during his nearly ten years in office. He argued that climate action must be at the center of all United Nations work because environmental issues drive conflict, cause people to leave their homes, and increase competition for land and water. As he prepares to leave his position at the end of December, his words served as a clear message to his successor about the importance of keeping the climate at the top of the global agenda.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《衛報》（The Guardian）報導，古特瑞斯在近十年的任期內，針對氣候變遷議題一直是一位立場鮮明的領導者。他主張氣候行動必須成為聯合國所有工作的核心，因為環境問題會引發衝突、導致民眾流離失所，並加劇對土地與水資源的爭奪。隨著他準備在十二月底卸下職務，他的這番話向繼任者傳達了一個明確的訊息，即必須將氣候議題置於全球議程的首位。

paragraphs.en: While Guterres spoke, most of the 90 world leaders who attended the summit had already returned to their home countries. This left negotiators to focus on the difficult work of creating a final agreement, often called a "cover decision." This document will outline the goals for the coming years. Key topics include the electrification of the global economy—using electricity instead of oil or gas for energy—and finding ways to help workers move from fossil fuel industries into cleaner jobs.
paragraphs.zh: 在古特瑞斯發言時，出席峰會的九十位世界領袖大多已返回各自國家。這使得談判代表們必須專注於制定最終協議的艱鉅任務，這份文件通常被稱為「總結決策」。該文件將概述未來幾年的目標，重點議題包括全球經濟的電氣化——即以電力取代石油或天然氣作為能源——以及尋找協助勞工從化石燃料產業轉型至更乾淨工作崗位的方法。

paragraphs.en: One of the most important goals for this year is a target to have 35% of the world’s energy come from electricity by 2035. Experts believe this is a vital step toward reducing carbon emissions. Other goals include cutting methane emissions and ensuring that developing countries receive enough financial support to deal with the disasters caused by climate change.
paragraphs.zh: 今年最重要的目標之一，是設定在二〇三五年將全球能源的百分之三十五轉為電力供應。專家認為，這是減少碳排放至關重要的一步。其他目標還包括削減甲烷排放，並確保開發中國家獲得足夠的財政支持，以應對氣候變遷所引發的災難。

paragraphs.en: A major development at the summit came from California Governor Gavin Newsom, the most prominent American politician present. The United States government, led by President Donald Trump, has chosen not to participate in this summit. However, Newsom told The Guardian that California is fully committed to moving away from oil, gas, and coal. He expressed support for the "Santa Marta coalition," a group of more than 50 countries that are working together to transition to solar, wind, and battery power.
paragraphs.zh: 峰會的一項重大進展來自加州州長紐森（Gavin Newsom），他是現場最受矚目的美國政治人物。由川普（Donald Trump）總統領導的美國政府選擇不參加此次峰會。然而，紐森向《衛報》表示，加州完全致力於擺脫石油、天然氣與煤炭。他對「聖塔瑪塔聯盟」（Santa Marta coalition）表達了支持，這是一個由五十多個國家組成的團體，正共同努力轉型至太陽能、風能與電池動力。

paragraphs.en: This coalition is significant because it is finding ways to move forward even when some countries try to block progress. In the past, certain nations that rely heavily on oil and gas have used rules about reaching a "consensus"—an agreement where everyone must say yes—to stop new climate plans. The Santa Marta coalition, which includes large economies like Germany, France, and Brazil, has decided to create its own roadmaps to end fossil fuel use. They hope that by showing success, other countries will eventually follow their lead.
paragraphs.zh: 這個聯盟之所以意義重大，是因為即使在某些國家試圖阻撓進展的情況下，它仍能找到前進的方法。過去，某些高度依賴石油與天然氣的國家，曾利用關於達成「共識」（即必須全員同意的協議）的規則來阻擋新的氣候計畫。包括德國、法國與巴西等大型經濟體在內的聖塔瑪塔聯盟，已決定制定自己的路線圖以終結化石燃料的使用。他們希望透過展現成功，讓其他國家最終能跟隨他們的腳步。

paragraphs.en: Former Maldives President Mohamed Nasheed praised this approach, suggesting that countries wanting to phase out fossil fuels should simply go ahead and do it rather than waiting for everyone to agree. The economic power of the countries in this coalition gives their plan a real chance of success. If they can prove that clean energy is both better for the climate and better for the economy, it could change the global energy market.
paragraphs.zh: 馬爾地夫前總統納希德（Mohamed Nasheed）稱讚了這種做法，並建議那些希望逐步淘汰化石燃料的國家，應該直接採取行動，而不是等待所有人達成共識。該聯盟成員國的經濟實力，使其計畫有真正的成功機會。如果他們能證明潔淨能源對氣候與經濟都有益，這將可能改變全球能源市場。

paragraphs.en: As the summit enters its final hours, there is a sense of both urgency and hope. The Australian co-presidency of the summit has released a list of reflections that will form the basis of the final agreement. While past summits have made progress—such as the 2021 agreement to "phase down" coal and the 2023 pledge to transition away from fossil fuels—the pressure remains high. Guterres reminded everyone that the future of the planet cannot be decided by those who profit from its destruction. As he leaves his role, his final request was simple: face the facts, follow the science, and never give up.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著峰會進入最後階段，現場瀰漫著一股急迫感與希望。擔任峰會共同主席的澳洲已發布了一份反映清單，這將構成最終協議的基礎。儘管過去的峰會已取得進展，例如二〇二一年達成「逐步減少」煤炭的協議，以及二〇二三年承諾轉型脫離化石燃料，但壓力依然巨大。古特瑞斯提醒所有人，地球的未來不能由那些從破壞中獲利的人來決定。在他卸下職務之際，他最後的請求很簡單：面對事實、遵循科學，且永不放棄。

keyTerms.definitionEn: Becoming impossible to manage or stop.
keyTerms.noteZh: 此片語常用於形容局勢惡化，而非字面上的旋轉。文中：Guterres warned that the climate crisis is spinning out of control.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To cause or influence something to happen or develop.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（駕駛），這裡指導致某種結果。文中：He argued that climate action must be at the center of all United Nations work because environmental issues drive conflict, cause people to leave their homes, and increase competition for land and water.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To stop something from moving forward or succeeding.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（街區、積木），這裡作動詞用。文中：This coalition is significant because it is finding ways to move forward even when some countries try to block progress.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To gradually stop using or producing something.
keyTerms.noteZh: 由動詞與介系詞組成，意思與單字原意不同。文中：Former Maldives President Mohamed Nasheed praised this approach, suggesting that countries wanting to phase out fossil fuels should simply go ahead and do it rather than waiting for everyone to agree.

Leaders are now focusing on renewable energy and financial support for vulnerable nations.

While scientists report a slight drop in fossil fuel emissions for 2026, they warn that total carbon output is still rising due to deforestation. The summit is taking place against a backdrop of high energy prices caused by the war in Iran. Activists and groups are calling for stronger action to protect workers and communities during the transition to clean energy. Meanwhile, the host nation, Turkey, has announced plans to expand its own fossil fuel production.

Reports suggest that current policies will lead to dangerous levels of global heating. Leaders are now under pressure to move away from fossil fuels and toward cleaner energy sources.

quiz.question: What is the specific target for global energy consumption mentioned in the article?

options.A: To have 50% of the world's energy come from renewable sources by 2030.
options.B: To have 35% of the world's energy come from electricity by 2035.
options.C: To transition 35% of the global workforce into clean energy jobs.
options.D: To reduce methane emissions by 35% before the year 2035.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第四段第一句明確指出：「One of the most important goals for this year is a target to have 35% of the world’s energy come from electricity by 2035.」選項 A 的 50% 與 2030 年皆為錯誤數據。選項 C 錯誤地將目標與「工作轉型」混淆。選項 D 雖然提到了甲烷減排，但文章並未將 35% 與甲烷減排連結，屬於混淆資訊的干擾項。

quiz.question: Why does the author suggest the 'Santa Marta coalition' is a significant development in climate politics?

options.A: Because it successfully convinced the United States to rejoin the climate summit.
options.B: Because it has enough financial resources to pay for all global climate disasters.
options.C: Because it bypasses the requirement for unanimous agreement that has previously stalled progress.
options.D: Because it is the first group to officially ban the use of oil and gas globally.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第六段與第七段，過去氣候協議常因「consensus」（共識決）規則被依賴化石燃料的國家阻撓，而 Santa Marta coalition 決定自行制定路線圖，不再等待所有人同意。選項 A 錯誤，因為美國並未參與。選項 B 文章未提及該聯盟有能力支付全球災難費用。選項 D 誇大了事實，聯盟是為了「轉型」，而非立即全面禁止化石燃料。

quiz.question: In the second paragraph, what does the word 'drive' mean in the phrase 'environmental issues drive conflict'?

options.B: To force someone to move to a new location.
options.C: To cause or motivate a process to happen.
options.D: To increase the speed of a physical object.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。在此語境下，「drive」意指「導致」、「推動」或「促成」。文章提到環境問題會引發衝突與資源競爭，因此是指環境問題是衝突背後的動力或原因。選項 A 是常見的字面意思，在此完全不適用。選項 B 雖然文章後文提到人們離開家園，但「drive conflict」並非指強迫搬遷。選項 D 雖然有「加速」之意，但在描述衝突的起因時，用「導致」更為精確。

quiz.question: Which statement best summarizes the main message of the article?

options.A: The COP31 summit was a complete failure because most world leaders left early.
options.B: António Guterres is retiring and plans to start his own climate coalition.
options.C: Despite political obstacles and the difficulty of reaching consensus, there is a push for urgent climate action through alternative coalitions.
options.D: The only way to save the planet is for every country to immediately stop using oil and gas.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。本文綜合報導了 COP31 的進展、Guterres 的警告，以及 Santa Marta coalition 如何透過繞過共識決來推動氣候行動，體現了在困境中尋求突破的主題。選項 A 過於偏頗，文章雖提到領導人離開，但仍強調談判持續進行。選項 B 錯誤，Guterres 並未提到要創立聯盟。選項 D 過於絕對，文章強調的是「轉型」（transition）與「階段性目標」，而非立即全面停止。
